the-story-of-a-white-rocking-horse: Laura Lee Hope, creator of the beloved Bobbsey Twins, wrote this gentle tale for very young readers. At its center is a handsome white rocking horse — a treasured toy whose adventures delight the children who love him. Told in simple language with a warm, old-fashioned charm, the story suits bedtime reading and early readers just finding their way with books.
seven-maids-of-far-cathay-being-english-: Mary Forman Ledyard taught in China and wrote these sketches from what she saw in her own classroom. Each chapter introduces a Chinese schoolgirl — her family, her lessons, her hopes — giving English readers a personal look at girlhood in early-twentieth-century China. The book is gentle and observant, valuing its young subjects as individuals rather than curiosities.
the-little-lady-of-the-big-house: Jack London's final novel unfolds on a great California ranch, where Dick Forrest has built an agricultural empire — and where his spirited wife Paula falls in love with his old friend Evan Graham. The triangle plays out among horses, harvests, and wide skies. Part romance, part hymn to the farming life London himself loved, it was the last book he finished.
poems-of-purpose: Ella Wheeler Wilcox — famous for Laugh, and the world laughs with you — gathers her most uplifting verse in this collection. Her poems urge courage, kindness, and perseverance in plain, musical language that millions loved. Though critics sniffed, ordinary readers took her words to heart, making her one of America's most quoted poets.
the-old-stone-house: Constance Fenimore Woolson — friend of Henry James and a fine novelist in her own right — sets this story in an old stone house heavy with memory. Her characters confront the past's hold on the present with quiet intensity. Woolson's subtle, observant fiction rewards readers who appreciate craft and psychological depth.
the-hero-of-hill-house: Mabel Hale's school story crowns its hero of Hill House — a boy whose pluck and honor win the day. Games, lessons, and tests of character fill these wholesome pages. A fine, clean tale for young readers. Through games bravely played and temptations resisted, he proves what a true Hill House boy should be.
good-sense: Baron d'Holbach's Good Sense — the bible of French atheism — argues for reason against religion in plain, forceful prose. Its calm radicalism shocked the 18th century. A classic of Enlightenment thought. Priests and kings found it dangerous; philosophers found it liberating.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-and-sch: This 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia article on the Abbey and School of Clonmacnoise — St. Ciaran's great Irish monastery on the Shannon — celebrates its golden age of learning. John Healy writes with patriotic warmth. A treasured reference on Ireland's monastic glory. High crosses still stand where the scholars once walked.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-melr: A 1913 entry on Melrose, the border abbey of Scotland. Bruce's heart lies in its choir. Michael Barrett recounts its ruined glory. Scott's moonlight made it famous. The heart of the Bruce was buried before its high altar. Its east window is the pride of the Borders.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbey-of-newh: The Encyclopedia on Newhouse, England's first Premonstratensian house. Lincolnshire's fens heard the white canons' chant. Francis Martin Geudens gives its story. A pioneer house of a new order. The order's English story starts at its Lincolnshire gate. Its canons wore white over black.
